# Workflow scripts — generated by Keel

These scripts are generated by Keel into `.claude/workflows/` alongside the project docs.
Each phase has a dedicated workflow script that creates one **phase branch** off `main` as its
integration point, fans out divisible work as parallel agents in separate `git worktree`s
branched off that phase branch, merges each task back into it, runs a mandatory doc-sync step
on it, then merges the phase branch — and only the phase branch — into `main`.

## Usage

Run a phase script:
```
# via Claude Code CLI
claude --workflow .claude/workflows/phase-N-<slug>.js

# or paste the path into the Workflow tool inside a Claude Code session
```

Run a standalone doc sync (before any manual merge):
```
claude --workflow .claude/workflows/doc-sync.js
```

## Scripts in this project

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `doc-sync.js` | Mandatory pre-merge doc sync — run after every unit of work |
| `phase-0-guardrails.js` | Phase 0: scaffold guardrails and CI |
| `phase-N-<slug>.js` | One script per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN phase |

## Rules

- Never merge to trunk without a doc-sync commit.
- Never merge a task branch straight to trunk — task branches merge into the phase branch;
  only the phase branch (code + doc-sync commit) ever merges to trunk.
- Never share a worktree between agents — one task, one worktree.
- Deferred items must state WHY and WHEN, not just WHAT.
- Decisions captured in ADR.md before merge, not after.
- Every task agent opens with `/goal` — a completion condition that blocks it from ending its
  turn early. Automated tests aren't enough: the condition also requires the `verify` skill to
  confirm the behavior end-to-end, plus a manual `claude-in-chrome` pass for UI work.
- What happens when a goal isn't met is a per-project policy, not a guess — see
  IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN's Standing rules for this project's chosen exit strategy (bounded retries,
  persistent-until-met, or escalate-on-first-failure). `/goal clear` is the deliberate escape
  hatch that policy uses to bail out — it is never a way to quietly fake completion.
